ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #15
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Where would you find facts about elephants? (1 mark)
   A. A junior encyclopaedia
   B. A timetable
   C. A form
   D. A calendar

2. Which information is a school detail? (1 mark)
   A. Your favourite food
   B. Your weight
   C. Name of the head teacher
   D. Your date of birth

3. What does the saying 'Unity is strength' mean? (1 mark)
   A. People are stronger when they work together
   B. Nobody needs friends
   C. The strongest person always wins
   D. Only leaders are strong

4. Which noun is always plural? (1 mark)
   A. cup
   B. book
   C. scissors
   D. spoon

5. /p/ is a whispered sound. /b/ is (1 mark)
   A. silent
   B. also whispered
   C. voiced, with a buzz
   D. a vowel

6. Which is a minimal pair for /p/ and /b/? (1 mark)
   A. pen, pain
   B. wet, wait
   C. men, main
   D. pig, big

7. 'She sighed with relief' means she (1 mark)
   A. was very angry
   B. was very tired
   C. was happy that a worry was over
   D. was afraid

8. Which letter is a tail letter? (1 mark)
   A. o
   B. t
   C. g
   D. m

9. What does 'bleed' mean? (1 mark)
   A. To lose blood from a cut
   B. To sing
   C. To eat too much
   D. To sleep

10. An underpass is (1 mark)
   A. a kind of train
   B. a bridge over a river
   C. a path or road that goes under a busy road
   D. a bicycle

11. Which closing is suitable for a friendly letter? (1 mark)
   A. Yours faithfully,
   B. Yours lovingly,
   C. Dear Sir,
   D. To whom it may concern,

12. A balanced diet is a diet that (1 mark)
   A. has only meat
   B. has only sweets
   C. has the right amounts of all types of food
   D. has no water

13. What is fluency? (1 mark)
   A. Not reading
   B. Reading very loudly
   C. Reading only one word
   D. Reading smoothly with few stops

14. You meet a new word while reading alone. What can you do? (1 mark)
   A. Skip the whole page always
   B. Ask nobody
   C. Throw the book away
   D. Use clues in the sentence and check a dictionary later

15. Where can you find pictures for a composition? (1 mark)
   A. Only on a calendar
   B. Only in a dictionary
   C. Only on money
   D. Books, magazines and websites with a teacher's help

16. Which sentence talks about a finished action in the past? (1 mark)
   A. Kamau bought data bundles yesterday.
   B. Kamau buys data bundles every week.
   C. Kamau will buy data bundles tomorrow.
   D. Kamau is buying data bundles now.

17. In the story 'The Boy and the Borrowed Phone', what did Otieno do with the strange message? (1 mark)
   A. He sent it to his class
   B. He replied at once
   C. He showed it to his aunt
   D. He typed his school name

18. What does the proverb 'A friend in need is a friend indeed' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Friends are only for games
   B. A true friend helps you when you are in trouble
   C. Friends should never ask for help
   D. A friend must be rich

19. Choose the correct -ing form of 'run'. (1 mark)
   A. running
   B. runing
   C. runnning
   D. runeing

20. Which pair of words differs only in /h/ and /f/? (1 mark)
   A. sit and seat
   B. cat and cap
   C. ship and sheep
   D. hill and fill

21. What does 'prevention' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Medicine that cures an illness
   B. A sharp object
   C. Acting so that something bad does not happen
   D. A kind of food

22. Which is a polite way to interrupt a speaker? (1 mark)
   A. Be quiet!
   B. Stop talking!
   C. You are wrong!
   D. Excuse me, may I ask a question?

23. What does 'for' mean when it is used as a conjunction? (1 mark)
   A. although
   B. before
   C. however
   D. because

24. Which sentence has the /ð/ sound in the first word? (1 mark)
   A. Thank the coach.
   B. Think before you act.
   C. The team practised hard.
   D. Three players scored.

25. Which question word asks about a thing or an action? (1 mark)
   A. whose
   B. what
   C. when
   D. where

26. Which is the best answer to 'When does the match begin?' (1 mark)
   A. It is mine.
   B. On the field.
   C. The referee.
   D. At ten o'clock.

27. Which sentence uses the correct form of the verb 'go' with the present perfect? (1 mark)
   A. They have gone to the river.
   B. They have go to the river.
   C. They have went to the river.
   D. They has gone to the river.

28. What does 'skimming' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Reading backwards
   B. Copying a passage
   C. Looking for one number
   D. Reading quickly to get the main idea

29. What comes after a preposition in a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. A noun or pronoun
   B. A question mark
   C. Another preposition
   D. A full stop

30. Which is the correct spelling of the evening meal? (1 mark)
   A. dinnar
   B. diner
   C. dinner
   D. dinnner

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Write the missing forms: good, better, ___ ; bad, ___ , worst; many, more, ___ . (3 marks)

32. Rewrite in the past tense: 'I watch a video and I learn a new word.' (2 marks)

33. Write two sentences beginning 'I would like to be' and give a reason in each. (3 marks)

34. Explain two ways to make a story interesting. (4 marks)

35. Write two reasons why people keep diaries. (2 marks)

36. Write three sentences about your family or school: one comparative, one superlative and one with two adjectives in the right order. (3 marks)

37. Explain how intonation can change the meaning of 'Really?' (3 marks)

38. Create a short puzzle with four clues whose answers are irregular plurals. (4 marks)

39. Tell in three sentences how to set up a reading club. (3 marks)

40. Describe the steps to interpret a picture. (3 marks)

41. When is it right to interrupt a speaker, and how should you do it? (3 marks)

42. Write two similes about food. (2 marks)

43. Underline the prepositions: 'The children ran along the road, past the bank and into the market.' (3 marks)

44. Give two differences between a friendly letter and an SMS. (2 marks)

45. Write three sentences about your classroom using some, any and many. (3 marks)

46. Name the three groups of food on a healthy plate and give one example of each. (3 marks)

47. Give two examples of regular plurals and two of irregular plurals. (2 marks)

48. Change to the past progressive: 'The children are singing in the hall.' (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #15 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — A junior encyclopaedia
   An encyclopaedia gives facts about many subjects.

2. C — Name of the head teacher
   School details include the school name, address and teachers.

3. A — People are stronger when they work together
   Working together makes a group stronger.

4. C — scissors
   Scissors are two blades joined together, so the noun is plural.

5. C — voiced, with a buzz
   The difference between p and b is the voice.

6. D — pig, big
   Pig and big differ only in the first sound.

7. C — was happy that a worry was over
   Relief is the feeling when a worry ends.

8. C — g
   G hangs below the line.

9. A — To lose blood from a cut
   A bleeding wound loses blood.

10. C — a path or road that goes under a busy road
   Pedestrians can walk through it without meeting cars.

11. B — Yours lovingly,
   Yours lovingly is friendly.

12. C — has the right amounts of all types of food
   It has energy, body-building and protective foods and water.

13. D — Reading smoothly with few stops
   Fluent readers read smoothly.

14. D — Use clues in the sentence and check a dictionary later
   Context and a dictionary help.

15. D — Books, magazines and websites with a teacher's help
   There are many safe sources.

16. A — Kamau bought data bundles yesterday.
   'Bought' and 'yesterday' show the action is finished.

17. C — He showed it to his aunt
   He remembered his teacher's advice and asked an adult.

18. B — A true friend helps you when you are in trouble
   A true friend is seen when we need help.

19. A — running
   Short verbs ending in one vowel and one consonant double the last letter.

20. D — hill and fill
   'Hill' begins with /h/ and 'fill' with /f/.

21. C — Acting so that something bad does not happen
   Prevention stops problems before they start.

22. D — Excuse me, may I ask a question?
   It is polite because it asks permission.

23. D — because
   'For' gives a reason.

24. C — The team practised hard.
   'The' has voiced 'th'; 'think', 'three' and 'thank' have unvoiced 'th'.

25. B — what
   'What' asks about things, ideas and actions.

26. D — At ten o'clock.
   'When' asks for a time.

27. A — They have gone to the river.
   The participle of go is gone.

28. D — Reading quickly to get the main idea
   Skimming gives the gist.

29. A — A noun or pronoun
   For example: 'on the table'.

30. C — dinner
   Dinner has a double n.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: best; worse; most
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: I watched a video and I learned (learnt) a new word.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for watched, 1 mark for learned/learnt.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: I would like to be a doctor because I want to help sick people. I would like to be a runner because I love sport.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence with reason, and 1 for accuracy.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Start with something that makes the reader curious, and add small details or similes. These help the reader picture the story and want to continue.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each way explained.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: To remember events; to practise writing; to record feelings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: My brother is taller than I am. He is the tallest boy in his class. He has a big round bag.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: A high rising voice shows surprise, while a low falling voice shows the speaker is not interested. So the tune of the voice shows feelings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way and 1 mark for linking to feelings.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: I have two of these and I walk on them: feet. You chew with these: teeth. Small animals that squeak: mice. Grown-up females: women.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each clue with a correct answer.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Agree on a regular time and a quiet place. Each member reads a book they have chosen. Take turns to tell the group about it and keep a list of the books read.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible sentence.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Look at the whole picture, read the caption, notice details and expressions, think what is happening and what will happen next.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three steps.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: When you did not hear or understand, or someone needs urgent help. Say politely: 'Excuse me, may I say something?'
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the reasons and 1 for a polite phrase.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: The bread was as soft as a pillow. The juice was as sweet as honey.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: along, past, into
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: A letter is longer and has five parts, but an SMS is short and has a receiver, a message and a sender. A letter is better for news and feelings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each difference.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: There are many desks in our classroom. We have some pictures on the wall. Is there any chalk?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Energy foods such as ugali; body-building foods such as beans; protective foods such as spinach.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group with an example.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Regular: books, dishes. Irregular: men, feet.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each pair.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: The children were singing in the hall.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for were, 1 mark for keeping singing.
